proposal.diagnosis: Zero outputs command joint midpoints, not the reset pose; all starts develop backward pitch and fall. Restore reset-pose biases and add symmetric tilt, angular-rate, and drift feedback. This initial repair remains unvalidated.

Zero outputs command joint midpoints, producing sag and backward collapse. The previous trial reduced pitch error but still allowed divergent translation. Restore neutral arm targets, support the knees, and strengthen damped balance feedback using tilt, velocity, and foot-relative position.

Zero outputs abandon the reset pose. Later trials improve height but retain divergent drift despite saturated ankles. Restore neutral arms and knee support; add hip velocity/support-centering feedback and joint-relative ankle correction. This repair remains unvalidated.

Both pitch directions diverge while feet remain planted; the 20-second case is fallen, not standing. Remove competing hip translation feedback, strengthen pitch restoration, and increase ankle support-centering and velocity feedback.

Fore-aft drift grows before ankle saturation despite sustained foot contact. Strengthen support-relative ankle restoration and velocity damping, adding modest hip compensation while preserving existing upright feedback.

Zero outputs command joint midpoints, followed by backward collapse without touchdowns. Restore native pose offsets and test pitch stabilization, forward-speed feedback, and bounded opposing leg responses driven by measured body state to initiate alternating steps; stability remains unverified.

Feet remain planted until pitch divergence; the lone touchdown occurs during collapse. Increase contact-driven opposing leg lift, coordinate ankle compensation, and revise velocity-dependent foot placement with stronger early pitch correction.

r01 remains mostly double-supported until pitching over; r02's larger excursions collapsed support. Try contact-sensitive alternating lift with modest hip amplitude, reverse hip speed feedback for corrective foot placement, and strengthen pitch damping without increasing knee excursions.

The retained policy mostly keeps both feet planted until pitching into a fall. Test stronger state-driven alternating lift with coordinated ankle motion, and reverse common hip feedback to advance foot placement during forward drift rather than retract both legs. Improvement remains unverified.

Current trials lose sagittal balance before sustained stepping; larger prior stepping attempts also fell backward. Strengthen hip pitch recovery and speed-error response, with modestly increased alternating leg motion and coordinated ankle compensation. This repair remains untested.

The checkpoint mostly retains double support until sagittal collapse; forward falling is not walking. This trial strengthens unloading of the non-support leg, reverses common hip speed feedback toward stance extension when underspeed, and modestly increases pitch stabilization. Sustained alternation remains unverified.

The checkpoint mostly keeps both feet planted until sagittal divergence; forward falling is not walking. This candidate biases flexion toward the unloaded leg, corrects feet drifting ahead of the pelvis, and revises speed feedback to encourage forward initiation with stronger braking.

The checkpoint remains mostly in double support, then falls; forward displacement is not sustained walking. This candidate strengthens state-driven alternating clearance, coordinates ankle compensation, and revises velocity feedback toward forward foot placement and braking. Stability remains unverified.

Pitch drift precedes falls; the retained policy produces no upright alternation. Strengthen sagittal recovery and speed-error response while modestly increasing reciprocal leg excitation and favoring flexion of the unloaded leg. This repair remains unverified.

Rollouts show pitch divergence and almost no upright alternation. Reverse common hip feedback to oppose divergence, strengthen ankle stabilization, and add contact-dependent swing excitation while preserving coordinated hip–knee–ankle amplitudes. This repair remains unvalidated.

All cases remain upright but settle into double support; target speed currently has no influence. Add forward demand and speed-sensitive, opposing roll-driven leg flexion to test unloading and alternating steps while retaining existing balance feedback.

The retained policy ignores target speed and settles into double support; r01 displaced the pelvis without stepping and fell. Test bounded, opposing roll-state leg flexion with modest forward drive, approximately preserving the standing offsets.

The retained checkpoint stands but ignores target speed and never steps; earlier trials fell without sustained alternation. Test smaller, reciprocal state-driven hip/knee motions with support-side weight transfer and reduced ankle saturation. Alternation and stability remain unverified.

The checkpoint ignores target speed and settles into double support; recent forward motion ended in falls without steps. Test bounded, opposing hip-velocity feedback with coordinated knee flexion, while reducing ankle position-feedback saturation and adding speed-command response. Sustained alternation remains unverified.

The checkpoint remains upright but ignores commanded speed and never steps; earlier large excursions caused falls. Test smaller bounded, opposing leg responses driven by foot separation, joint velocity and contact, with modest command-dependent ankle drive. Alternation and stability remain unverified.

The checkpoint ignores target speed and settles into double support; recent attempts fell without sustained alternation. Test bounded, speed-sensitive opposing leg feedback with coordinated knee clearance and lateral transfer, while reducing swing-foot contamination of ankle feedback. Stability remains unverified.

The checkpoint stands but ignores speed; recent stepping trials show backward collapse and ankle saturation. Reduce shared foot-position coupling, add forward speed drive, and test bounded roll-responsive alternating leg flexion while retaining existing lateral stabilization.

The checkpoint ignores target speed and settles into double support. Earlier stepping trials overreached while ankles saturated. Try bounded, speed-sensitive reciprocal leg flexion with smaller hip excursions, forward drive, and reduced swing-foot contamination of ankle feedback; sustained alternation remains unverified.

The checkpoint ignores target speed and settles into double support. Earlier stepping trials overreached and fell backward. This update attempts smaller, body-state-driven alternating flexion, adds forward drive, and reduces swing-foot contamination of bilateral sagittal feedback. Stability remains unverified.

The checkpoint ignores commanded speed and settles into double support. Earlier trials either tipped without stepping or alternated while retreating. This unvalidated edit adds bounded, body-state-driven opposing knee/hip responses and forward command coupling, while reducing ankle sensitivity to advancing feet.

Standing works, but speed commands have no effect. Preserve all existing balance coefficients; test modest forward drive and bounded roll-responsive reciprocal leg motion. Added terms cancel exactly at zero command. Walking and stopping from motion remain unverified.

Standing passes; the latest trial only shifts double-support equilibrium without stepping. Preserve existing balance feedback and exactly cancel added terms at zero command. Test stronger forward demand with bounded, roll-state-driven reciprocal leg unloading; walking and transitions remain unverified.

Standing works; commanded stepping previously overreached, saturated ankles, and collapsed backward. This unvalidated update preserves the zero-command mapping exactly, adds smaller reciprocal flexion and forward demand, and continuously reduces bilateral foot-position coupling as command increases.

Standing works, but the checkpoint ignores speed. Previous stepping attempts developed excessive roll, overreach and ankle saturation. Test smaller bounded reciprocal leg responses and modest forward demand, retaining shared balance feedback. Added terms cancel exactly at zero command; walking and stopping remain unverified.
